items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-07-29
items.q: I was crazy for George Brackey. I thought he was one of him and the big idol.

ctx.x: What kind of a clarinet player was Georgie Boyd? John Boyd was a pretty good clarinet player. Would you say he had a rough style?

Well yeah his style was more rough than I was. Rougher than you? Yeah. He's a hard clarinet player. Was he strong? He's pretty strong. But I got to lean on all of them. I didn't ask for it or say I had it. They gave it to me. On Hale I didn't know. After I was playing a whole lot of clarinet. And that time. They had a good little clarinet play some of them boys. I can't remember. Who were the ones that you liked especially? In clarinet? Well the one I liked in clarinet really was uh. I say for instance you say…
Walter Barnes was away? Where was he from? He was from St. Charles or Lake Charles. He got killed in a fire.

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: Now you see, I learned from Piku, George.

ctx.x: Later years. But the force would come now. Now you see, I learned from Piku, George. But my ideas were from Lloyd. Now Big R. Louis was a man that played a clarinet. And he could take a clarinet and make a rooster, curl, dog bark, anything like that. And that's why I learned he told him that problem. Right on the end, because if he was playing the hill, I wouldn't dance or go out there. I wouldn't have to hang him or nothing from him.
Would you say he was your favorite of all the ones you heard?
